Annotations, Lines & Arrows

geom_text, geom_label, ggrepel, ggtext, reference lines, segments, curves and arrows

Add text, labels, rich-text annotations, reference lines, segments, curves and arrows to ggplot2 plots. Covers geom_text, geom_label, ggrepel, ggtext, geom_vline, geom_hline, geom_abline, geom_segment, and geom_curve.

Text annotations — geom_text()

geom_text() adds plain text at specified coordinates or mapped from data.

library(ggplot2)

# Add a single annotation at fixed coordinates
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(x = 4.5, y = 30,
                label = "High efficiency zone"),
            stat = "unique",
            colour = "steelblue", size = 4)

# Label each data point from a column
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars))) +
  geom_point(colour = "tomato") +
  geom_text(size = 2.5, nudge_y = 0.4)

# Customise size, colour, face, angle
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(x = 2, y = 15,
                label = "Important note"),
            stat  = "unique",
            size  = 5,
            colour = "red",
            fontface = "bold",
            angle = 10)
Note

Set stat = "unique" when adding a single annotation to avoid it being drawn once per data row.

Labels with background — geom_label()

geom_label() works like geom_text() but draws a filled rectangle behind the text, making it easier to read on busy plots.

library(ggplot2)

# Single label
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(aes(x = 4.5, y = 30,
                 label = "Target region"),
             stat  = "unique",
             fill  = "#fff3cd",
             colour = "darkorange")

# Label every point
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg,
                   label = rownames(mtcars))) +
  geom_point(colour = "#e84855") +
  geom_label(size = 2.2, fill = "white",
             label.size = 0.3,
             label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"))

# Custom colours
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(aes(x = 2, y = 15,
                 label = "Economy cars"),
             stat  = "unique",
             size  = 5,
             colour = "red",
             fill   = "green")

Non-overlapping labels — ggrepel

ggrepel automatically repositions labels so they don’t overlap each other or the data points.

install.packages("ggrepel")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# geom_text_repel
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars))) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 20)

# geom_label_repel (with background box)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars))) +
  geom_point(colour = "tomato") +
  geom_label_repel(
    size          = 2.8,
    box.padding   = 0.35,
    point.padding = 0.5,
    fill          = "white",
    label.size    = 0.25,
    max.overlaps  = 15
  )

# Label only selected points
library(dplyr)
top <- mtcars |> filter(mpg > 25 | wt < 2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = top, colour = "#e84855", size = 3) +
  geom_label_repel(data = top,
                   aes(label = rownames(top)),
                   size = 3, fill = "white")

Rich text — ggtext

ggtext allows Markdown and HTML in plot text via element_markdown() and geom_richtext().

install.packages("ggtext")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtext)

# Markdown in title and labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "**Weight** vs *Fuel Economy* by <span style='color:#e84855'>Cylinders</span>",
    x     = "Weight (1,000 lbs)",
    y     = "Miles per Gallon"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(size = 14)
  )

# geom_richtext — HTML/Markdown in annotations
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_richtext(
    aes(x = 4.5, y = 30,
        label = "**Economy zone**<br><span style='color:grey'>mpg > 25</span>"),
    stat       = "unique",
    fill       = "white",
    label.colour = "steelblue"
  )

# Coloured axis labels with element_markdown
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e84855","#2d6be4","#12a36a")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "4" = "<span style='color:#e84855'>**4 cyl**</span>",
    "6" = "<span style='color:#2d6be4'>**6 cyl**</span>",
    "8" = "<span style='color:#12a36a'>**8 cyl**</span>"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_markdown(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

General annotations — annotate()

annotate() is a versatile function for adding shapes, text, and lines without a data frame.

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()

# Text
p + annotate("text", x = 4.5, y = 30,
             label = "Annotation text",
             colour = "tomato", size = 5, fontface = "bold")

# Rectangle (shaded region)
p + annotate("rect",
             xmin = 1.5, xmax = 2.5,
             ymin = 25,  ymax = 35,
             alpha = 0.15, fill = "steelblue")

# Segment
p + annotate("segment",
             x = 2, y = 20,
             xend = 3, yend = 25,
             colour = "red", linewidth = 1,
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3,"cm")))

# Point
p + annotate("point", x = 3.5, y = 20,
             colour = "red", size = 5, shape = 18)

# Label box
p + annotate("label",
             x = 4, y = 32,
             label = "Outlier zone",
             fill = "#fff3cd", colour = "darkorange")

Reference lines

Vertical lines — geom_vline()

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))

# Single vertical line
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = 2)

# Multiple vertical lines
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 0, 1),
             linetype    = 1,
             colour      = 2:4,
             linewidth   = 0.8)

# Vertical line at the mean
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 12, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mtcars$mpg),
             colour = "tomato", linetype = 2, linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean(mtcars$mpg) + 1.5, y = 7,
           label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean(mtcars$mpg), 1)),
           colour = "tomato", hjust = 0)

Horizontal lines — geom_hline()

# Single horizontal line
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = 2)

# Multiple horizontal lines
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 0, 1),
             linetype   = 3,
             colour     = 4,
             linewidth  = 1)

Diagonal lines — geom_abline()

# y = x line (identity line)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1,
              colour = "tomato", linetype = 2)

# Custom regression line
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = coef(model)[1],
              slope     = coef(model)[2],
              colour    = "steelblue", linewidth = 1)

Segments & arrows — geom_segment()

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))

# Basic segment
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_segment(x = -1, y = 0, xend = 1, yend = 1,
               colour = 2, linewidth = 1)

# Arrow
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_segment(
    x     = -2, y    = 1,
    xend  =  1, yend = -1,
    colour    = 2,
    linewidth = 1,
    arrow     = arrow(length = unit(0.4, "cm"),
                      type   = "closed")    # "open" or "closed"
  )

# Annotation with segment + label
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(x = 1.6, y = 33, xend = 1.88, yend = 30.4,
               colour = "#e84855",
               arrow  = arrow(length = unit(0.3,"cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.45, y = 33.5,
           label = "Most fuel-efficient",
           colour = "#e84855", size = 3.5)

Curves — geom_curve()

geom_curve() draws a curved line instead of straight — useful for callout arrows.

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))

# Basic curve
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_curve(x = -2, y = 1, xend = 1, yend = -1,
             colour = 4, linewidth = 1)

# curvature: 0 = straight, negative = left, positive = right
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_curve(x = -2, y = 1, xend = 1, yend = -1,
             colour     = 4,
             curvature  = -0.3,
             linewidth  = 1)

# Curved arrow annotation
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_curve(
    x = 1.55, y = 35, xend = 1.86, yend = 30.9,
    colour    = "#e84855",
    curvature = -0.25,
    arrow     = arrow(length = unit(0.3,"cm"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.3, y = 35.5,
           label = "Toyota Corolla", colour = "#e84855", size = 3.5)

Quick reference

Function Purpose Key args
geom_text() Plain text labels label, size, colour, angle, nudge_y
geom_label() Text with background box label, fill, label.size
geom_text_repel() Non-overlapping text (ggrepel) max.overlaps, box.padding
geom_label_repel() Non-overlapping labels (ggrepel) fill, label.size
geom_richtext() HTML/Markdown text (ggtext) label, fill
element_markdown() Markdown in theme elements Use in theme(plot.title = ...)
annotate() Ad-hoc shapes & text "text", "rect", "segment", "label"
geom_vline() Vertical reference line xintercept, linetype, colour
geom_hline() Horizontal reference line yintercept, linetype, colour
geom_abline() Diagonal reference line intercept, slope
geom_segment() Line segment / arrow x,y,xend,yend, arrow
geom_curve() Curved segment / arrow curvature (-1 to 1), arrow
